items.title: 30.2 NMR spectroscopy ke solvents (ghol banane wale liquids) (Roman Urdu)

blocks.text: ¹H NMR mein jis sample ko analyse (check) karna ho use zyada (excess) solvent mein ghol kar solution banaya jata hai. Aam solvents mein hydrogen atoms hote hain jo strong (tez) signals dete hain aur sample ke spectrum mein interference (rukawat) dalte hain. Is masle se bachne ke liye deuterated solvents use kiye jate hain, jaise CDCl₃ (deuterated chloroform) ya CD₃OD (deuterated methanol). Agar aam CHCl₃ solvent ho to us ke single (akele) proton (¹H) ka signal itna strong hoga ke sample ke protons ke weak (kamzor) signals ke oopar aa kar (overlap ho kar) unhein bilkul chhupa dega. CDCl₃ mein hydrogen (H) ki jagah us ka isotope deuterium (D) hai. Deuterium ko flip karne ke liye radio waves ki different frequency chahiye, is liye yeh sample ko di gayi radio frequency absorb nahi karta aur ¹H NMR spectrum mein is ki peak nahi aati. Is tarah solvent "silent" (khamosh) rehta hai aur spectrum mein sirf sample ke signals nazar aate hain.

blocks.prompt: ¹H NMR mein CHCl₃ ki jagah CDCl₃ kyun use hota hai?
blocks.explanation: CHCl₃ ke proton ka strong signal sample ke weak signals ko chhupa deta. CDCl₃ mein H ki jagah D hai, jo ¹H wali frequency absorb nahi karta, is liye solvent ki koi peak nahi aati.

items: Aam solvents ke hydrogen strong signals de kar sample ke signals chhupa dete hain.
Deuterated solvents (CDCl₃, CD₃OD) ¹H spectrum mein silent (khamosh) rehte hain.
